title: Named Individual Subjects: Árpád and the Seven Chieftains

sections.content: So far your multi-subject narration has used group nouns as the subject — 'a rómaiak' (the Romans), 'a hunok' (the Huns). Now the story introduces a NAMED individual, Árpád, alongside a group, 'a hét törzs' (the seven tribes) or 'a törzsek vezetői' (the tribes' leaders). Keep the same rule as before — verb number must match its subject — but now watch carefully which sentence has an individual (singular) and which has the group (plural).

sections.title: Individual vs. group as subject
rows: Árpád led the tribes. (singular subject, singular verb)
The tribes' leaders united. (plural subject, plural verb)
Árpád was elected prince. (lit. 'they elected Árpád prince' — no stated subject)

items.spanish: A hét törzs vezetői vérszerződéssel egyesültek egyetlen közös vezetés alatt.
items.english: The leaders of the seven tribes united under one common leadership by a blood oath.

items.spanish: A hagyomány szerint elsőként Álmost választották fejedelemmé, ám végül a fia, Árpád vezette be a törzseket a Kárpát-medencébe.
items.english: According to tradition, Álmos was elected prince first, but in the end it was his son Árpád who led the tribes into the Carpathian Basin.

items.spanish: Az Árpád-ház, amelyet Árpád alapított, közel négyszáz évig uralkodott Magyarországon.
items.english: The Árpád dynasty, which Árpád founded, ruled Hungary for nearly four hundred years.

sections.content: Hungarian often expresses a passive-like meaning ('X was elected/chosen/founded') simply by using a 3rd-person-plural verb with no subject stated: 'Álmost választották fejedelemmé' literally means 'they elected Álmos prince', but is understood as 'Álmos was elected prince' — nobody specific is meant by 'they'. This is one of the most useful tools in Hungarian for narrating history without naming who exactly did the choosing.
